learning: If s-bend and slalom max_error falls below 0.061 m, or those runs progress further, while line losses stay at 0, lower yaw inertia is helping edge correction. If oval progress falls below 0.5 or oval oscillation exceeds 0.33, revert mass to 0.8 kg. If drift persists unchanged at 0.061 m, the limit is controller response at the edge, and kp is the next integrator lever.
notes: Builder's iteration 8 candidate: iteration 5 geometry with mass reduced from 0.8 kg to 0.6 kg. The controller is unchanged from iteration 5 so the race isolates the mass effect.
rationale: Iteration 7 (inner sensors at ±0.04 m) was rejected: oval progress fell to 0.22, oval line losses rose to 1.9 per run, and s-bend and slalom losses returned to 1.0. The Builder's current candidate returns to the iteration 5 geometry (best measured, 151.9) and changes only total mass from 0.8 kg to 0.6 kg. Sensor layout (outer ±0.06 m, inner ±0.03 m, y 0.04 m, 12 mm footprints), wheel_track 0.12 m and wheel_radius 0.03 m are unchanged, so any change in edge drift or progress comes from lower yaw inertia. Iteration 5 has zero s-bend and slalom line losses and fails only by drifting to the 0.06 m edge (max_error about 0.061 m) while still reading the tape. A lighter body should turn faster for the same wheel command. The controller is kept exactly at the iteration 5 gains (kp 1.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.0, last_direction, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]). This isolates the mass effect, and the 0.6 kg change leaves the existing damping in place. The main risk is more oval oscillation (0.327 at 0.8 kg, above the 0.3 target), so the Builder's revert rule at oval progress below 0.5 applies. I do not change kp or kd now, because raising kp would confound the mass test and could worsen oscillation. Expected result: s-bend and slalom max_error below 0.061 m or those runs progressing further, with line losses still at 0 and oval progress near 0.7.
